item.title: How the $p$-Bergman metric approaches the Carath\'eodory metric
item.description: arXiv:2611.08616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rate at which the $p$-Bergman metric approaches the Carath\'eodory metric on convex domains with measures comparable to $\delta^\alpha dV$, $\alpha>-1$. On smooth convex domains of finite type the logarithmic coefficient is bounded above by the harmonic-measure average of the tangential multitype dimension plus $1+\alpha$, with equality when almost every endpoint of the extremal disc is coercive. For a class of convex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with $C^4$ boundary and rank-one real tangential contact along an axis disc, a winding number distinguishes the coefficient $2+\alpha$ from an upper bound $7/4+\alpha$; quartic contact makes the latter bound exact. The exact value holds along the entire axis of explicit real-algebraic strongly pseudoconvex domains, including perturbations without the weighted circle action, although their pointwise boundary models agree up to unitary equivalence with those of a domain having coefficient $2+\alpha$. A $C^2$ example has negative winding but coefficient $2+\alpha$, with a $-\frac12\log\log p$ correction, so boundary regularity is essential to the gap theorem.
item.dc:creator: Gunhee Cho

item.title: McShane's identity and the Brownian loop measure
item.description: arXiv:2611.08687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We combine McShane's identity for a once-punctured torus with the length-spectrum identity of Wang and Xue. An exact identity in each primitive homology class yields a finite limit for the difference of two divergent length-spectrum sums over self-intersecting hyperbolic geodesics. The limit is $\frac18$ and is equivalent to McShane's identity. We also derive higher-iteration identities governed by integer divisors.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Slice Regular Capacity and Rational Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Approximation theory in the complex plane is a well established area of mathematical research, with extensive contributions documented in the literature, notably through the classical results of Weierstrass, Runge, Mergelyan, and Vitushkin. Approximation theory in quaternionic settings, particularly rational approximation on compact sets, which studies when slice regular functions can be uniformly approximated by rational functions, is one of the recent areas of interest in quaternionic rational approximation theory (See [6,13]). In this paper, we discuss Vitushkin approximation theorem in the quaternionic setting by using the quaternionic analogue of analytic capacity and also we establish Davies modified Vitushkin scheme in quaternionic setting. We also discuss quaternionic analogue of $\gamma_{+}$- capacity and Cauchy capacity and the remarkable results of Tolsa [35] and Younsi [45] related to these capacities in complex plane setting.
item.dc:creator: Thankarajan Prasad, Rincy Susan Raju, Enose Shine Lal

item.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_{\beta}$ to $A^p_{\alpha}$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_{\beta}$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_{\beta}$. Moreover, $A^q_{\beta} \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_{\beta}$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_{\gamma}] \subset [T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.
item.dc:creator: Zengjian Lou, Jinbang Wen

item.title: Centralizers of elliptic univalent self-maps and the embeddability problem in the unit disc
item.description: arXiv:2611.08944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\phi$ be an elliptic univalent self-map of the unit disc in the complex plane that is not an automorphism, with multiplier $0<|\lambda|<1$ at its Denjoy--Wolff point. The simultaneous Schr\"oder linearization of maps commuting with $\phi$ is classical. Using this linearization, we identify its univalent centralizer with the multiplicative semigroup of scalars that preserve the Koenigs domain, and investigate how the geometry of this semigroup controls continuous-time embeddings. We show that the identity is a non-isolated point of the centralizer precisely when the centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup; such a semigroup need not contain $\phi$. For each logarithmic branch $\mu_k=-\mathrm{Log}\lambda+2\pi i k$, we establish a local sector alternative that characterizes the existence of an embedding with spectral value $\mu_k$. We prove that the set of admissible branch indices is either empty, a finite interval of integers, or all of $\mathbb{Z}$, and give examples realizing all three possibilities. Finally, we describe the full holomorphic centralizer, including the constant map with value equal to the Denjoy--Wolff point.
item.dc:creator: Akira Mino

item.title: A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(\theta,\mu)$, where $\mu$ is a positive Radon measure and $$\theta=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $\mu$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators. Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $\mu$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.
item.dc:creator: Bowoo Kang, Jaechul Lee, Zhenghao Li

item.title: Period bounds for Bergman kernel variation and the Suita defect
item.description: arXiv:2611.09341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The periods of holomorphic differentials give an explicit lower bound for the curvature of Bergman evaluation matrices. We prove this bound along the Green sublevels of a smooth plane domain. For scalar evaluation at the Green pole, equality at one regular level holds precisely when that sublevel is simply connected. For complete jets at the Green pole, the matrices have continuous first derivatives, including at critical levels, and their logarithmic determinant defects are integrals of nonnegative curvature densities. A further estimate bounds the accumulated period energy by the determinant defect, with a constant independent of the jet order. On a multiply connected domain, all these defects vanish up to the first critical Green value and become strictly positive above it.
item.dc:creator: Fusheng Deng, Gang Huang, Kefeng Liu

item.title: Ahlfors $1$-Regularity and Conformal Criteria for Carleson Measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.09467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a bounded Jordan domain $\Omega$ has Ahlfors $1$-regular boundary if and only if the following criterion holds for every positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$: $\mu$ is Carleson exactly when $\int_\Omega |\phi'(w)|\,d\mu(w)<\infty$ for every conformal bijection $\phi$ from $\Omega$ onto a bounded domain with rectifiable boundary. The same characterization holds using only arclength measures on simple locally rectifiable curves, with the integral condition replaced by finite length of every such conformal image. These results extend Bishop's theorem on the unit disk. We also study analogous criteria for vanishing Carleson measures.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Hou, Huaying Wei

item.title: Divergence Rates for Orbits of Semigroups of Holomorphic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior for forward and backward orbits of one-parameter semigroups of holomorphic self-maps of the unit disk. For both types of orbits, we determine the asymptotic growth rate of hyperbolic length and compare it with the total speed of the semigroup, obtaining sharp constants that depend on the intrinsic properties of the semigroup and on the starting point. In the process, we discover new characterizations for standard notions in the theory of semigroups. We further explore, from a potential theoretic scope, the rate by which compact sets in petals of semigroups degenerate to a boundary point in the backward dynamical setting.
item.dc:creator: Maria Kourou, Konstantinos Zarvalis

item.title: Finite-Scale Folding and Maximal Asymptotic Variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Regular multi-types and the Bloom conjecture II
item.description: arXiv:2611.09823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ $(n\geq2)$ be a smooth pseudoconvex real hypersurface. We prove that, for every $1\leq s\leq n-1$, the regular $s$-contact type, the $s$-commutator type, and the $s$-Levi type coincide at every point of $M$, thereby resolving Bloom's conjecture in any dimension. The solution in dimension three was obtained in 2021 by the second and the third authors. Moreover, for any smooth rank $s$ subbundle $B\subset T^{1,0}M$, we establish the equality of the commutator type and the Levi type associated with $B$, giving an affirmative answer to the generalized D'Angelo conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqing Chen, Xiaojun Huang, Wanke Yin, Pingsan Yuan

item.title: Cantor's onion: a uniformly quasiregular map whose Julia set is a Cantor set of spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.08773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For integers $d,m\ge2$ with $1/d+1/m<1$, we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{S}^3$ of degree $d^2+m^2$ whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps $z^d+\lambda/z^m$, built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension $2+s$, where $d^{-s}+m^{-s}=1$, and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy $\log(d^2+m^2)$. We also prove that uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set, possibly with branching there, have no wandering domains and only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all of them attracting basins. The map constructed here belongs to this class.
item.dc:creator: Alastair N. Fletcher, Gaven J. Martin

item.title: Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman spaces are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map
item.description: arXiv:2611.09731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we consider weighted Bergman spaces over open unit disk corresponding to nonnegative integrable radial functions with positive mass arbitrarily close to the unit circle. Then we show that Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the weighted Bergman space are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map. This result generalizes the classical characterization of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space due to Brown and Halmos. Moreover, we prove that there is no compact Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman space.
item.dc:creator: Samir Panja

item.title: Multiplicity-Weighted Moments of a Two-Monomial Harmonic Map Beyond the Caustic
item.description: arXiv:2609.28370v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While the Jacobian of a planar harmonic mapping keeps a constant sign, the signed and the unsigned area elements agree up to that sign, and the two natural moment hierarchies coincide. Once the Jacobian changes sign the critical circle acquires a caustic as its image, part of the plane is covered several times with opposite orientations, and the hierarchies part company: integrating a radial weight against $J_F$ lets overlapping sheets cancel, giving the degree-weighted moments $J_n$, while integrating against $|J_F|$ lets every sheet count positively, giving the multiplicity-weighted moments $J_n^{\pm}$. These are the classical degree and area formulas for the same map, the second weighted by the multiplicity function (Banach indicatrix). It is the second family, the one the caustic threatens, for which a closed form is no longer automatic. For the two-monomial map $F(w)=w+iC\bar w^{k}$ on an annulus we show that it has one anyway: $J_n^{\pm}$ is the total variation of the very same explicit primitive whose endpoint difference gives $J_n$. Crossing the caustic therefore costs exactly one extra evaluation point, the critical radius $r_*=(k|C|)^{-1/(k-1)}$, and it is the same point for every order $n$: the weight $|F|^{2n}$ is nonnegative and so contributes no sign change of its own. On the degree-weighted side $J_n$ has a boundary-only closed form for every $n\ge0$, the zeroth being the signed area of the image counted with degree, and the complex-weighted moments vanish unless $(k+1)\mid(m-\ell)$. Neither weighted integral is a new object, and the caustic of this family has been located before in the literature on harmonic trinomials; what is new is the closed evaluation of the multiplicity-weighted hierarchy across it.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as B\'odis

item.title: Local Characterizations of Oka Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10475v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that strong dominability, the LAP, and the Oka property are equivalent for complex manifolds. The proof turns approximation across an attached disc in one complex variable, uniformly in holomorphic parameters, into convex approximation in arbitrary dimension. We also characterize Oka manifolds by the LEP, formulated in terms of centered holomorphic families of discs. In dimension $n\geq1$, LEP propagates across sets of zero $(2n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The Oka property is local in the Euclidean topology, and it descends under surjective holomorphic maps between connected complex manifolds. Deformations of very free rational curves give the Oka property for every smooth connected complex projective rationally connected manifold $X$, and for $X\setminus A$ whenever $A\subset X$ is a closed algebraic subset of codimension at least two. Compact K\"ahler manifolds admitting a K\"ahler metric with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature, or having nef tangent bundle, are also Oka. For $n\geq1$, the complement of a smooth hypersurface $D\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ is Oka if and only if $d\leq n+1$.
item.dc:creator: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.13831v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.
item.dc:creator: Gordon Heier, Ravi Mudaliar, Haotian Zuo

item.title: Modular Existential Closedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.35409v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Aslanyan

item.title: On the Hodge Extension of Local K\"ahler Forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.38055v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a Stein manifold, and let $K=\{h\le0\}$ be a compact sublevel set of a strictly plurisubharmonic function $h$ defined near $K$. It is known that $K$ is meromorphically convex in $X$ if and only if $dd^ch$ extends to a Hodge form on $X$. We show that if $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the direct sum of a free abelian group and a torsion group, for example if it is finitely generated or if $X$ is a Stein surface, then any extension of $dd^ch$ to a K\"ahler form on $X$ can be modified, after replacing $h$ by a positive multiple, into a Hodge form. Thus, meromorphic convexity of $K$ is equivalent to the extendability of $dd^ch$ as a K\"ahler form. We also show that the topological assumption cannot be dropped: we construct a Stein manifold $X$ of dimension $6$ with $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Q$, a sublevel set $K$ as above that is not meromorphically convex although $dd^ch$ extends to a K\"ahler form, and a totally real torus in $K$ that is isotropic for a K\"ahler form but is not meromorphically convex. This shows that the Hodge condition in Guedj's characterization of meromorphically convex totally real submanifolds cannot be weakened to a K\"ahler condition, and gives counterexamples to two criteria stated by Cieliebak and Eliashberg.
item.dc:creator: Rasul Shafikov

item.title: Commutation relations for two-sided radial SLE
item.description: arXiv:2405.07082v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the commutation relation for 2-radial SLE in the unit disc starting from two distinct boundary points. We follow the framework introduced by Dub\'{e}dat~[12]. Under an additional requirement of the interchangeability of the two curves, we classify all locally commuting 2-radial SLE$_\kappa$ for $\kappa\in (0,8)$: it is either two-sided radial SLE$_\kappa$ with spiral of constant spiraling rate or chordal SLE$_\kappa$ weighted by a power of the conformal radius of its complement. Namely, for fixed $\kappa$ and starting points, we have exactly two one-parameter families of locally commuting 2-radial SLE curves. We also discuss the semiclassical limit of the commutation relation as $\kappa \to 0$. In particular, we show that the limit for the second family with an appropriately chosen power of the conformal radius is a chord that minimizes a modified chordal Loewner energy, which is unique only when the endpoints are not antipodal.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Krusell, Yilin Wang, Hao Wu
